clue.text: Injure one's skin

parts.note: to cut someone is to injure them
one is I, and the 's is S, so one's gives IS

explanation.surface: A warning that someone has hurt their own skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Cutis is the anatomical term for the skin, the true skin or dermis.

clue.text: Chartism's campaigning for annual festival

indicators.note: campaigning suggests agitation, so the letters of the movement's name are stirred up

explanation.surface: The Chartist movement lobbying for a yearly celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: Chartism was a nineteenth-century British working-class movement for political reform.
explanation.definitionFit: Christmas is the yearly festival celebrating the birth of Jesus.

clue.text: Bet a piranha will eat a mammal

indicators.note: will eat signals that the letters are swallowed inside the words bet a piranha

explanation.surface: A wager that the fish will devour an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A tapir is a hoofed mammal of tropical America and Asia with a short trunk.

clue.text: Difficult to get hold of, like a mule?

definitions.meaning: hard to grasp, like a wet fish or an elusive person
a mule is a backless shoe, a kind of slipper, so slipper-like

explanation.surface: A stubborn mule that wriggles free.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mule' suggests the animal but is a backless slipper.
explanation.definitionFit: Slippery means hard to hold, and whimsically means slipper-like, as a mule shoe is.

clue.text: Shrewd walker heading west around a northern port

parts.note: arch means knowing or shrewd
the a is taken as written; around is only a loose joining word placing it beside the other pieces

indicators.note: in an across entry, heading west means the word leg is read right to left

parts.note: a leg is what one walks with

explanation.surface: A canny hiker turning west to skirt a harbour in the north.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across entry 'heading west' means reading right to left. Archangel (Arkhangelsk) is a Russian port on the White Sea; 'northern' is wordplay, not part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Archangel is a major seaport in the far north of Russia, on the White Sea.

clue.text: Against Dickensian villain being beheaded

indicators.note: being beheaded means the villain's name loses its first letter

parts.note: Fagin is the villain of Oliver Twist by Dickens

explanation.surface: Opposing a Dickens villain's execution.
explanation.definitionFit: Agin is a dialect form meaning against or opposed to.

clue.text: Agreement regarding structure in metropolis

indicators.note: in places the regarding and structure letters within the metropolis word

parts.note: a metropolis is a large city
on means regarding, as in a talk on art
form means shape or structure

explanation.surface: A deal about the design of a big city.
explanation.definitionFit: Conformity is compliance or accordance with rules or with others, a form of agreement.

clue.text: Shocks friend, stuck in part of church briefly

indicators.note: stuck in places the friend inside the shortened church part
briefly means the church part is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: an apse is a recess at the end of a church
a pal is a friend

explanation.surface: A buddy wedged in a church alcove gets a fright.
explanation.definitionFit: To appal is to horrify or dismay, so appals means shocks.

clue.text: Family member unwell in village after vacation somewhere in Normandy

parts.note: gran is a grandmother, a family member

indicators.note: in puts the unwell letters inside the emptied village
after vacation means the village word is vacated, keeping only its outside letters

parts.note: ill means unwell

explanation.surface: A grandmother falls ill in a French village after her holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vacation' looks like a holiday but means emptying the word village to VE.
explanation.definitionFit: Granville is a seaside town on the Normandy coast of France.

clue.text: Shortly acquire knowledge involving Hungary's principal composer

indicators.note: involving means the shortened word wraps around that letter
shortly means the learning word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: to learn is to acquire knowledge

indicators.note: principal means the first letter of the country's name

explanation.surface: A quick lesson on Hungary's leading composer.
explanation.walkthrough: Franz Lehár was Hungarian, composer of The Merry Widow.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz Lehár was a Hungarian-born composer of operettas, notably The Merry Widow.

clue.text: Like a snake? Traveller hit it, reversing

parts.note: a rep is a travelling sales representative

indicators.note: reversing tells us the words hit it are read backwards

parts.note: to nail something is to hit it squarely

explanation.surface: A salesman runs over a snake while backing his car.
explanation.definitionFit: Snakes are reptiles, so something snake-like is reptile-like; the question mark marks the definition by example.

clue.text: Fruit and vegetable chart

parts.note: a pea is a vegetable
CH is an abbreviation for chart

explanation.surface: A nutrition chart listing fruit and vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: A peach is a soft stone fruit with downy skin.

clue.text: Recaps unusual predicament

indicators.note: unusual signals that the letters of recaps are arranged in an uncommon way

explanation.surface: A sports report summarising an odd tight spot.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrape is an awkward or difficult situation, a fix or jam.

clue.text: Send six balls towards the wicket? Wow!

definitions.text: Send six balls towards the wicket?
definitions.meaning: in cricket an over is six balls, so to bowl an over is to send six deliveries
to astonish or overwhelm someone, as an exclamation of amazement suggests

explanation.surface: A cricket commentator marvelling at a bowler's spell.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled from one end.
explanation.definitionFit: Bowl over is an idiom for amazing someone, and literally describes delivering an over in cricket.

clue.text: About end of the war, friend turned out to be emergency worker

indicators.note: about means the rearranged friend goes around the other letters
turned out means the letters of friend are turned into a new order
end of means take the final letter of the

explanation.surface: A friend who became a firefighter at the war's close.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned out' rearranges the letters of 'friend' into FIRDEN, which 'About' then wraps around E and WAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A fire warden watches for and responds to fires, an emergency role, especially in wartime.

clue.text: Dress mom in pants? They're said to be up to date

definitions.text: They're said to be up to date

indicators.note: pants is British slang for rubbish, so the letters of dress mom in are rubbish and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Putting your mother in trousers, presumably to keep her fashionable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pants' looks like a noun for trousers but is British slang for rubbish, the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Modernisms are contemporary expressions or usages, regarded as current and fashionable.

clue.text: Initially deputy head keeps register: that's very amusing

indicators.note: keeps means the opening letter and headland hold the register inside
initially means just the first letter of deputy

parts.note: a ness is a headland, a head jutting into the sea
a roll is a register or list of names

explanation.surface: The deputy head taking the register is a source of fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deputy head' reads as a school role, but is split.
explanation.definitionFit: Drollness is dry wit or humour, the quality of something that amuses.

clue.text: Great number massacred

definitions.meaning: a large quantity, as in a whole lot of things
past tense of slay, meaning killed in large numbers

explanation.surface: A grim report of many killed.
explanation.definitionFit: Slew means a large amount informally, and is also the past tense of slay.

clue.text: News about a sea-mist coming up in Irish port

indicators.note: about means the news word goes around the other letters

parts.note: word means news, as in send word

indicators.note: in a down entry, coming up means the sea-mist word is read upwards

parts.note: a fret is a sea mist on the English east coast

explanation.surface: A report of fog rolling in over an Irish harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Waterford is a port city in the south-east of Ireland.

clue.text: Very old, prudish woman left behind

indicators.note: behind places the left letter after the woman

parts.note: prim means prudish
Eva is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A prim old lady who was left behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left behind' reads as abandoned, but is L placed after EVA.
explanation.definitionFit: Primeval means belonging to the earliest ages, so extremely ancient.

clue.text: Sinatra's first record, a big hit

indicators.note: first means take only the opening letter of the singer's name

parts.note: a log is a written record, as a ship's log

explanation.surface: Frank Sinatra's debut single was a chart smash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a big hit' sounds like chart success but means a heavy blow, as in cricket slogging.
explanation.definitionFit: A slog is a hard wild swing, especially a big hit in cricket.

clue.text: Guarantee time at hospital dept will lead to a cure?

parts.note: you bet is a guarantee, so a bet stands for an assurance
a term is a period of time
ENT is the ear, nose and throat department of a hospital

explanation.surface: A promise that a spell in a hospital ward will cure you.
explanation.definitionFit: Betterment is improvement, and a cure is an improvement in health, loosely the same thing.

clue.text: Gradually take in summary of news

definitions.meaning: to absorb information slowly, as a meal is broken down
a condensed collection of news reports

explanation.surface: Slowly absorbing a news round-up.
explanation.definitionFit: Digest means absorb or assimilate, and also a compilation summarising news or writings.

clue.text: Old musician's dirty-sounding vehicle

indicators.note: sounding says the word for making dirty is taken by how it is said, not spelt

parts.note: to sully is to make dirty
a van is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A former musician's grubby-looking tour van.
explanation.walkthrough: Arthur Sullivan was the Victorian composer of the Gilbert and Sullivan operettas.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Arthur Sullivan was a nineteenth-century English composer, so an old musician.

clue.text: Small drink knocked over — display of anger results

indicators.note: knocked over means the drink is turned upside down, read upwards in this down entry

parts.note: port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: Spilling a small drink leads to a tantrum.
explanation.definitionFit: A strop is British slang for a sulk or bad-tempered fit.

clue.text: Writer, one who risks losing capital

indicators.note: capital here is the initial letter, which the gambler word loses

parts.note: a gambler is one who takes risks

explanation.surface: An author who stakes money and loses it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing capital' suggests losing money but means dropping the first letter. Eric Ambler wrote spy thrillers.
explanation.definitionFit: Eric Ambler was a British author of thrillers such as The Mask of Dimitrios.

clue.text: See about making connection with new Italian star

parts.note: lo is an old word for see or look
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Watch for a new Italian celebrity making contacts.
explanation.definitionFit: Sophia Loren is a celebrated Italian film actress, a screen star.

clue.text: Run away fast, for the most part

indicators.note: for the most part means all but the last letter of the fast word

parts.note: fleet means fast or swift

explanation.surface: Escape quickly, mostly.
explanation.definitionFit: To flee is to escape or run off from danger.

clue.text: Official participating in more events

indicators.note: participating in means the letters are taking part within the run of more events

explanation.surface: A referee or steward taking part in extra fixtures.
explanation.definitionFit: A reeve was a local magistrate or officer in medieval England, a kind of official.

clue.text: Company with consignments of French meat and eggs?

parts.note: de is French for of
liver is a meat
O looks like an egg, so OO is eggs

explanation.surface: A firm that ships French meat and eggs abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: Deliveroo is a British food delivery company.
explanation.definitionFit: Deliveroo is a food delivery firm, a business built on dropping off orders.

clue.text: Maybe perfect tapes sent for review

indicators.note: sending tapes for review suggests reworking them, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Recordings posted to a critic who may judge them flawless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perfect' looks like praise but is a grammatical tense, as in 'I have written'.
explanation.definitionFit: The perfect is one form of past tense in grammar, hence the 'maybe' signalling an example.

clue.text: Entering refurbished deli, number formed a queue

indicators.note: entering means the number letter goes inside the rearranged shop letters
a refurbished shop has been redone, so the letters of deli are rearranged

explanation.surface: Customers queued on entering a newly renovated delicatessen.
explanation.definitionFit: To line up is to stand in a row, so lined can mean formed a queue.
